title: TreatmentSuppressed.v1
description: A selected treatment was NOT executed because an execution guardrail blocked it (plan §6.5 catalogue extension, §7 DEC-14/DEC-16). Emitted by treatment-service on `collections.treatment` keyed by `caseId` when the state machine goes to SUPPRESSED. The guardrails re-evaluated immediately before dispatch are: a fresh customer-policy fetch (unavailable ⇒ `POLICY_RECHECK_UNAVAILABLE`, fail closed), the channel's contact window, and the frequency caps — so a customer who set do-not-contact between the decision and the dispatch is not contacted, which is the entire reason the re-check exists. Suppression is a first-class outcome with reasons, not a silent drop: it is counted in dashboards and is the evidence for "why did the strategy decide to contact but nothing was sent?".

treatmentId.description: Identity of the treatment that was suppressed — the aggregate this event is about. The treatment row survives in SUPPRESSED state; it is never deleted, because the fact that a contact was intended and blocked is itself auditable.

decisionId.description: The decision that selected the suppressed treatment, so a suppression can be traced back to the strategy that intended it.

caseId.description: Collection case the treatment belonged to, and the partition key.

suppressionReasons.description: Every guardrail that blocked the dispatch, as registry reason codes — ALL of them, not just the first: a treatment blocked by both a contact window and a frequency cap must show both, or the operator who fixes the window will not understand why nothing changed. Codes come from registries/reason-codes.v1.json (category EXECUTION for guardrail blocks, POLICY for a customer-policy block found at re-check). Never empty.
